newsitem.title: LEBANON: BANK SHARES "BLUE CHIP" OF BEIRUT MARKET.
newsitem.headline: BANK SHARES "BLUE CHIP" OF BEIRUT MARKET.

text.p: Banque Audi touched again on Wednesday its alltime high of $23 while Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce traded for the second day at a record $17.5.
"The bank shares are the blue chip stocks of the bourse. They are keeping liquidity in the market," a broker, who wished not to be identified, told Reuters.

Banque Audi fell during the first two days of the week to $22.25 in what some dealers said was "temporary profit-taking". On Wednesday, a big bloc of 58,868 shares changed hands at $22.25 on the exchange.
A second bloc of 30,000 shares which traded at the same price off the BSE a day earlier was declared on Wednesday.
"Audi is fundamentally good. Price of the share should reach a minimum of $26-$27 by the end of the year," the broker said.
Bank of Beirut, the third bank listed, was unchanged at $3.625.
Brokers say that BLC, trading at $17.5, was drawing interest from institutional investors and that the stock should keep its upward trend.
"As for BLC, it should be consolidating between $17.5 and $18. At $17.25 and $17.5, the share is a good buy. We might see some profit-taking as the share touches $18-$18.25 levels," the broker said.
All three banks traded in heavy demand.
Solidere shares were unchanged. A shares traded at $10.5 while B shares traded at $10.75 for the second consecutive day. Demand for both shares exceeded supply.
Of the four listed industrial firms, Ciments Libanais and pipemaker Eternit traded unchanged at $1.28125 and $1.875 respectively.
There was no trading in Ciments Libanais or tilemaker Uniceramic.
The LIBX bank index rose 1.11 percent to 147.67. The BLOM general index rose 0.13 percent to 930.55 and the LISPI general index rose 0.3 percent to 88.33.
Total BSE turnover was 231,677 shares for a value of $3,241,500 compared with 200,550 shares for a value of $2,129,428 a day earlier.
